answer: A plan I have for the near future is to pursue further studies abroad, which has been a long-held ambition of mine. Ideally, I would like to do a master's in management, probably in the UK or Australia. I made this decision fairly recently, after realising that international experience would greatly benefit my career. Ironically, it was helping other students with their applications every day that finally convinced me to take the step myself. To carry it out, I have been researching universities, preparing for the required exams and saving diligently, since it is quite an [[ambitious]] undertaking. At the moment, I am working on my IELTS, practising a little every evening after work. The process is genuinely demanding, but I am approaching it in a [[methodical]], step-by-step way. My younger sister has been a great help too, quizzing me on vocabulary over dinner. This plan is important to me because I believe studying in a different country would be a hugely [[enriching]] experience, both academically and personally. It would push me out of my comfort zone and expose me to new perspectives. Honestly, the thought of it is both exciting and slightly nerve-wracking, especially the idea of being so far from my family. I know there will be challenges along the way, but I am fully committed to [[seeing it through]]. It represents a significant investment in my future, and I am determined to make it a reality, so that I can come back with skills that are genuinely [[transferable]].

followUps.q: How does your family feel about your plan?
followUps.answer: They are proud but a little emotional about it. My mother worries about me living alone, while my father keeps reminding me that opportunities like this don't come twice, so I should grab it.

followUps.q: Would you come back to Bangladesh afterwards?
followUps.answer: Yes, I think so. My family is here, and I would like to use what I learn to help young people from towns like mine. Gaining experience abroad first would be a real bonus, though.

note: Specified the course and destination, the irony of advising others, IELTS preparation and family feelings; plain 'committed' mark moved to [[seeing it through]], added [[transferable]].
